# Package options

## Overview
teems provides a set of advanced options that control package behavior across function calls.
For example, teems is rather chatty and users may wish to silence all innocuous messages with `ems_option_set(verbose = FALSE)`.
Options are managed through three functions:

- `ems_option_get()` retrieves current option values
- `ems_option_set()` modifies option values
- `ems_option_reset()` restores all options to their defaults

```r
ems_option_get(
  name = NULL
)

ems_option_set(
  tempdir = NULL,
  verbose = NULL,
  ndigits = NULL,
  accuracy_threshold = NULL,
  accuracy_figures = NULL,
  accuracy_criterion = NULL,
  full_exclude = NULL,
  check_shock_status = NULL,
  timestep_header = NULL,
  n_timestep_header = NULL,
  docker_tag = NULL,
  assertions = NULL,
  range_test_initial = NULL,
  range_test_updated = NULL,
  random_seed = NULL,
  refine = NULL,
  converge = NULL
)

ems_option_reset()
```

Options persist for the duration of the R session and are reset on package reload.

## Retrieving options

View all current options:
```r
ems_option_get()
```

Retrieve a specific option by name.
An error is raised if the name is not a valid option:
```r
ems_option_get("verbose")
ems_option_get("ndigits")
```

## Setting options

One or more options can be set in a single call:
```r
ems_option_set(verbose = FALSE)
ems_option_set(verbose = FALSE, ndigits = 8)
```

## Resetting options

Reset all options to their default values:
```r
ems_option_reset()
```

## Available options

| Option | Default | Description |
|--------|---------|-------------|
| `tempdir` | `tempdir()` | Directory used for temporary file storage during a model run |
| `verbose` | `TRUE` | If `FALSE`, function-specific diagnostics are silenced |
| `ndigits` | `6` | Number of digits to the right of the decimal point kept when data are written to file. Values smaller than 0.1 in magnitude keep `ndigits` significant digits instead, so small nonzero data (e.g. `1e-10`) are not rounded to zero |
| `accuracy_threshold` | `0.8` | Share of results that must be accurate to at least `accuracy_figures` significant figures. A warning is generated if the share is lower |
| `accuracy_figures` | `4` | Significant figures, from 1 to 6, a result must reach to count as accurate |
| `accuracy_criterion` | `"solution"` | The accuracy summary judged: `"solution"` the levels values of the endogenous results, `"data"` the values read from data files and updated, `"both"` the two together. A run that updates no data is judged on the solution |
| `full_exclude` | `c("DREL", "DVER", "XXCR", "XXCD", "XXCP", "SLUG", "EFLG")` | Headers to fully exclude from all aspects of the model run. Failure to designate these headers properly will result in errors. Modify with caution |
| `check_shock_status` | `TRUE` | If `FALSE`, no check on shock element endogenous/exogenous status is conducted |
| `timestep_header` | `"YEAR"` | Header written with the time of each period, as given in `time_steps` of `ems_data()` (years, or steps from the initial period); the model uses the differences between periods as interval lengths. For novel intertemporal models — modify with caution |
| `n_timestep_header` | `"NTSP"` | Header written with the number of periods (the length of `time_steps`). For novel intertemporal models — modify with caution |
| `docker_tag` | `"latest"` | Tag of the `teems` image to solve with |
| `assertions` | `"fatal"` | Severity of TAB `Assertion` failures during [`ems_solve()`](solve.qmd): `"fatal"`, `"warn"` or `"off"` |
| `range_test_initial` | `"fatal"` | Severity of declared-range violations (e.g. `(ge 0)`) on initial values, read or computed: `"fatal"`, `"warn"` or `"off"` |
| `range_test_updated` | `"warn"` | As `range_test_initial`, for updated values |
| `random_seed` | `1` | Seed of the TAB function `RANDOM(a,b)`. The same seed gives the same draws on every run; each Formula element keeps its draw across solution steps. Change the seed for a new sequence (GEMPACK instead draws a new sequence per run by default) |
| `refine` | `TRUE` | One refinement step after every `"DBBD"` linear solve, which brings its accuracy to that of `"LU"`. It holds the system matrix through each solve, and the memory estimate counts it; `FALSE` turns it off. `"LU"` and `"SBBD"` are backward-stable and need no refinement; `"NDBBD"` is not refined, as it cannot yet keep its factorization for a second solve |
| `converge` | `FALSE` | `TRUE` applies GEMPACK's treatment of poorly converging results to runs extrapolated from three solutions: the result with the most steps where the three do not converge cleanly, their average where they are nearly equal. Not available with subtotals |
